SYNTHETIC — BoE MPR press conference transcript (June 2026), built to mirror
the structure of the official BoE PDF transcript:
  * turn-based dialog with standalone capitalized name labels (no ALL-CAPS
    roles, no Question:/Answer: markers)
  * opening remarks are a separate PDF; the transcript opens with the tail of
    the Governor's closing remarks
  * wrapped lines and page breaks fall between turns and sometimes mid-sentence
    (page-spanning turns must be accumulated before mining)
  * a single-word interjection ("Yeah.") and a wrapped PDF fragment
    ("Charter Act.") must never be treated as speaker labels
  * journalist questions carry numeric claims that are never mined
  * a quoted third party is never attributed to an MPC member

==== PAGE 1 ====
Andrew Bailey
So with that, Dave, Clare and I will be happy to take your questions. Thank you.
Katie Martin
Should we do Mehreen and then Ed.
Mehreen Khan
Governor, markets appear to be pricing rate cuts next year. Is GDP really expected to grow by about 1.5 percent this year?
Andrew Bailey
We took a decision today to leave Bank Rate unchanged, and that is the relevant conclusion.
==== PAGE 2 ====
Clare Lombardelli
Yeah.
On activity at the moment is we judge it to be relatively weak. So it was about 0.1%
growth in the last quarter. That's obviously below what we would expect supply to be.
So you've got weakness there.
Andrew Bailey
And it's about those pieces of data and how they all interact with each other that
will form the judgment on where rates need to go.
Tim Wallace
Does the Committee see the risks to inflation as tilted to the upside?
Dave Ramsden
10-year gilt yields have risen by about 350 basis points. I think we've been very
clear that we see the balance of risks on inflation tilted to the upside.
Andrew Bailey
There will be a decision in September, as there always is, and we will announce it.
Inflation is expected to average 2.1 percent in 2027.
Unemployment is projected to average 4.5 percent.
One researcher told us that the natural rate may have risen, but we do not share that view.

Andrew Bailey
And it really reflects this, that our balance sheet is split into two parts by the 1844 Bank
Charter Act.
So we have what's called the Banking Department and the Issue Department.
Financial conditions have tightened notably over the course of this year.
Huw Pill
We remain vigilant.
